key_insight: After mild traumatic brain injury, many older adults recover well by 6 months, but the oldest patients and those with pre-injury cognitive impairment have much worse outcomes.
clinical_relevance: 6-month functional prognosis after mTBI in older adults is strongly shaped by age and baseline cognition, which may help identify patients needing closer follow-up and support.
method: Prospective cohort at two U.S. level I trauma centers
Older adults seen within 72 hours of mTBI with head CT and co-enrolled informants
Outcomes tracked with GOSE at 2 weeks and 6 months, with weighting to reduce attrition bias
evidence_signal: In 253 participants, 14% died by 6 months, 73% were home independent, and 17% achieved complete recovery; GOSE was more sensitive than ADL or FAQ for detecting change.
watch_item: This was a cohort study with attrition and some unknown pre-injury cognitive status, so the findings support prognosis rather than proving which interventions improve recovery.
paper_title: 6-Month Recovery after Mild Traumatic Brain Injury in Older Adults: A TRACK-GERI Study
